Is there a 24-hour pharmacy on Koh Samui? | Very few street pharmacies stay open all night, and hours change often. After about 22:00, go to a private hospital emergency department, where a doctor can see you and the hospital pharmacy dispenses 24 hours. 7-Eleven sells basics such as paracetamol and plasters around the clock.
Can I buy antibiotics without a prescription in Thailand? | Many pharmacies will sell common antibiotics on request, but it is better to see a doctor first. Most holiday infections are viral, the wrong antibiotic won't help, and a clinic visit gives you the right drug and a receipt for your insurer.
Can I bring my prescription medicine to Thailand? | Yes for everyday medicines, in original packaging with a prescription or doctor's letter, and only enough for your trip. Controlled medicines such as strong opioids and some ADHD or sleeping drugs may need a Thai FDA permit before travel, so check a month ahead.
Where can I buy seasickness tablets on Koh Samui? | Any pharmacy in Chaweng, Lamai, Bophut, Maenam or Nathon sells dimenhydrinate-based seasickness tablets. Take one 30–60 minutes before your boat leaves, not after you start to feel sick.
Do pharmacists on Koh Samui speak English? | In the tourist areas most pharmacists speak enough English to help, and many signs are in English. Show the generic name of the medicine or a photo of your packaging to avoid confusion over Thai brand names.
Can I buy CBD on Koh Samui? | Only FDA-approved CBD products can be sold legally, and extracts above 0.2% THC are narcotics. Cannabis flower needs a Thai prescription. Many products on sale don't meet the rules, and you must never take cannabis or CBD products out of Thailand.
What should I bring for a boat trip? | Seasickness tablets taken before departure, reef-safe mineral sunscreen (chemical filters are banned in national parks such as Ang Thong), a hat, water, your regular medicines in a dry bag, waterproof plasters and water shoes.
